name: Memory Map Viewer
blurb: flash and RAM region use as a scaled strip
intro: Paste the output of arm-none-eabi-size (-A for per-section addresses, or the default Berkeley line) and give the memory regions from your linker script. Each section is placed in the region its address falls in, and .data is counted twice: in RAM, and as its load copy in flash. The strips are drawn to scale.

inputs.label: Memory regions
inputs.help: As in the linker script's MEMORY block; lengths like 512K or 0x80000.

inputs.label: Size output
inputs.placeholder: arm-none-eabi-size -A firmware.elf  (or name size region per line)

examples.title: Small STM32F030 with the Berkeley line

input.sizes:
text    data     bss     dec     hex filename
  14820     120    2952   17892    45e4 blinky.elf

usage: Give the memory regions (name, origin as 0x hex, length like 512K) and paste the output of arm-none-eabi-size -A (or -A -x), the default Berkeley size line, or lines 'name size region'. It returns each region's use in % and bytes, a section table with addresses, result.regions (parts with offsets, for the drawing), and warnings when a region overflows or is over 90 % full. Use it to see how close a firmware is to its flash or RAM limit.
sources: GNU binutils size(1): Berkeley and System V formats
GNU ld manual §3.6.8.2 output section LMA (load copies of initialised data)
